author: Aaronjacobs000
summary: These parsers read HashiCorp Vault audit log entries from a Vault audit device, forwarded over syslog to the data collector. Logins go to Auth and every other API call goes to CloudAudit; request entries stay in generic, so each call is counted once.
notes:
Setup:
- Turn on a Vault audit device and forward its lines to the Sophos NG-SIEM data collector over syslog.
- The syslog device (vault audit enable syslog) writes to the local syslog agent with tag vault; forward from there over TCP, since large entries overflow a UDP packet.
- HashiCorp suggests the file device read by a forwarder instead (vault audit enable file file_path=...), which also works.

Field mapping:
- The parser takes the JSON object at the end of each line, with or without a syslog header or an audit prefix.
- Vault logs each API call twice, as a request entry and a response entry.
- Response entries go to the children and request entries stay in generic, so each call is counted once.
- Logins (auth/<mount>/login, OIDC callbacks) go to Auth.
- Every other call (secret reads and writes, encryption, policies, mounts, audit devices, tokens) goes to CloudAudit with the operation as the event name, the mount type as the event type and the API path as the resource.
- Vault writes an HMAC of most string values, including token accessors, so session_id and access_key hold hashes unless the device sets hmac_accessor=false.

Made up in the samples:
- Samples follow the audit log entry schema in HashiCorp's docs with made-up values; they leave out the hashed client_token and secret values, which the parsers don't read.

Testing:
- Each child, combined with the parent into one parser, passed Run Test in a lab tenant on 2026-10-14 (150 of 150 fields matched the emulator in each of 3 runs), and the parent's confirm string picked the same lines there.
- Each child also passed Run Test as a separate parser under its parent (148 of 148 fields, each line taken in 5 of 5 runs).
- No built-in parser claimed these lines.
